items.grounds: Re-derived at byte tier from oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5 (14 tokens; atnach on token 7, יִזְכְּר֑וּךָ): the second half opens on הֵן אַתָּ֤ה קָצַ֨פְתָּ֙ (tokens 8-10), second-person address in the same person as the first half's opening verb פָּגַ֤עְתָּ (token 1), so the person of address does not change across the caesura; the only new element is the first-person-plural confession verb וַֽנֶּחֱטָ֔א (token 11), WEB “Behold, you were angry, and we sinned.” (web:Isa.64.5 = oshb:Isa.64.4). First-person-plural verbs already stand inside the preceding row's span: הָיִ֗ינוּ (oshb:Isa.63.19 = web:Isa.63.19, the split verse's first half, token 1; WEB “We have become”) and נְקַוֶּ֑ה (oshb:Isa.64.2 = web:Isa.64.3, token 4; WEB “we didn’t look for”) -- no morphology layer is staged, so the form class rests on the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings. Tested the other way, the row's underlying seam fact holds: skeleton-tier sweeps of the sin, iniquity and transgression roots spliced from oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5, oshb:Isa.64.5 = web:Isa.64.6 and oshb:Isa.59.20 return 23, 16 and 18 verses book-wide with none inside oshb:Isa.63.15-Isa.64.3 (= web:Isa.63.15-Isa.64.4), so the confession onset at oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5 survives and the finding is right to leave the span alone. The warrant's stated contrast (second-person address versus first-person-plural admission) is byte-defective as a distinguishing ground, while the seam does not rest on that contrast alone: medium, as filed. Non-span item; the proposed field repair (rest the contrast on the confession verb alone and drop the person-shift framing) is consistent with the bytes.

Re-derived at byte tier from oshb:Isa.64.11 = web:Isa.64.12 (8 tokens): the verse reads הַעַל אֵ֥לֶּה תִתְאַפַּ֖ק יְהוָ֑ה (tokens 1-4, atnach on token 4) and then תֶּחֱשֶׁ֥ה וּתְעַנֵּ֖נוּ עַד מְאֹֽד (tokens 5-8); the interrogative he stands only on token 1, הַעַל, and the second colon's verb תֶּחֱשֶׁ֥ה carries no interrogative particle of its own, so the Hebrew is one interrogative governing two cola. WEB renders it “Will you hold yourself back for these things, Yahweh? Will you keep silent and punish us very severely?” (web:Isa.64.12 = oshb:Isa.64.11) with two question marks, and that WEB run is the row's only citation for its 'final unanswered double question' and for the observed_substrate_signals entry speech_formula.unanswered_closing_question: the row splices no Hebrew at its own closing verse and none at oshb:Isa.65.1, whose verse-initial first-person form נִדְרַ֨שְׁתִּי֙ (byte tier) is the actual tier-1 speaker change it invokes. Tested the other way, the closure survives on the bytes (the interrogative particle, the first-person reply at oshb:Isa.65.1, and the SAMEKH the inventory records at MT 64:11 -- single-witness, tier-3), so the seam is not load-bearing on the punctuation; but a seam-relevant device whose 'double' count is a translation-punctuation fact and whose closing verse carries no pointed splice is a defective warrant under the tier-4 law: medium, as filed. Non-span item; the proposed field repair (splice the particle and atnach position, or re-label the signal key) is consistent with the bytes.

Byte check of the shared seam oshb:Isa.64.3 | oshb:Isa.64.4 (= web:Isa.64.4 | web:Isa.64.5): oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5 opens on the second-person verb פָּגַ֤עְתָּ (byte tier) with no vocative, no messenger frame and no speaker or addressee change from oshb:Isa.64.3 = web:Isa.64.4, and the paragraph-mark inventory records no petuchah or setumah at MT 64:3 or MT 64:4 (single-witness; absence is not counterevidence), so both rows' description of the seam as a rhetorical-mode shift rather than a formal header is byte-true. The incoherence is real as filed: this row sets frontier_flag_considered false while its own device_notes calls the onset 'a soft, tonal seam rather than a formal header' and the neighbour row on the other side of the same seam flags exactly that ground true at the same medium_low confidence. Downgraded from medium to low because the flag is a disclosure field, not a warrant, digit or mark claim: the row's boundary argument, its medium_low confidence and its rival disclosure already carry the seam's softness in prose, and the neighbour's true flag at the identical seam already routes the question into the frontier queue, so the shortfall is a mechanical one-field inconsistency with no effect on the boundary or its evidence. Non-span item; the proposed one-field repair (set the flag true) is consistent with the bytes.

Re-derived at byte tier: oshb:Isa.65.17 (14 tokens) opens on כִּֽי (token 1) and carries הָרִ֣אשֹׁנ֔וֹת at token 10; oshb:Isa.65.16 (18 tokens) carries the byte-identical form at token 15 and closes on מֵעֵינָֽי (token 18). A sweep at that pointed form returns 2 verses book-wide at byte tier (MT 65:16, 65:17), 3 accent-stripped (adding MT 41:22) and 5 skeleton (adding MT 42:9, 48:3), so the row's digit, its 'pointed form' qualifier and its byte-identity claim all re-verify exactly. The position wording is nonetheless byte-false: the noun neither closes the unit's final verse (three tokens follow it) nor opens the next verse, and the row's own next clause names the true verse-initial token, כִּֽי, contradicting itself. The claim lives in the rejected-alternative's cross-seam disclosure, not in the seam driver (the koh-amar onset at oshb:Isa.65.13 and the subject shift at oshb:Isa.65.17 stand independently), so it is a byte-false claim that is not load-bearing: medium, as filed. Non-span item; the proposed position-neutral rewording is consistent with the bytes.

Re-derived at byte tier: oshb:Isa.66.2 (20 tokens) carries נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה at tokens 9-10 with the atnach on token 10, and the verse continues וְאֶל זֶ֣ה אַבִּ֔יט (tokens 11-13) inside the same declaration; the inventory records no petuchah or setumah at MT 66:2 (single-witness; absence not counterevidence). Skeleton-tier sweeps spliced from those tokens: the two-token formula returns 19 verses book-wide, the bare signature 23 -- the finding's 23 is the bare-signature object, not the two-token formula, a count-object slip that does not touch its claim. Every other check on the row re-verifies: verse-initial כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה at oshb:Isa.66.1 (byte tier), SAMEKH at MT 65:25 and MT 66:4 under the claimed type (single-witness), and the trembling root spliced from oshb:Isa.66.5 returning 7 verses book-wide at skeleton tier. Downgraded from medium to low: the row's ground says 'no intervening tier-1 seam', and at row granularity a seam is a verse boundary; a signature standing mid-verse on the atnach with the declaration continuing past it is not seam-eligible, so the rejection ground is byte-true as a seam claim (the finding itself concedes the span survives). What remains is a disclosure shortfall -- a tier-1-class formula inside the span goes unmentioned while oshb:Isa.66.2 is cited for other content -- which is mechanical rather than a defective warrant. Non-span item; the proposed positioned restatement is consistent with the bytes.

Re-derived from the bytes: the three-token opener ק֤וֹל שָׁאוֹן֙ מֵעִ֔יר spliced from oshb:Isa.66.6 (tokens 1-3) returns 1 verse book-wide at byte, accent-stripped and skeleton tiers (MT 66:6 only) -- a hapax at every tier. The bare opener ק֤וֹל (token 1) returns 31 verses as a skeleton substring, of which exactly 5 carry it as the verse-initial token (MT 13:4, 40:3, 40:6, 52:8, 66:6). The row's sentence attaches '(sweep: 5 verses book-wide at that verse-initial opener, skeleton tier)' directly to the three-token splice, so the digit's stated object (the quoted phrase) and its true object (the one-word verse-initial herald opener) differ; the count-discipline law requires the swept object to be named before the digit. The digit sits in the rejected-alternative's rival disclosure and the rejection rests on content, so the misbinding is not load-bearing: medium, as filed. Non-span item; the proposed repair (name the one-word object, keep the phrase as the byte splice with no digit attached) is consistent with the bytes.

Re-derived from the bytes: oshb:Isa.66.6 opens verse-initially on ק֤וֹל (byte tier), one of exactly 5 verse-initial herald openers book-wide (skeleton tier; MT 13:4, 40:3, 40:6, 52:8, 66:6), a signal class the owner-ruled strategy lists as tier-1; its 10 tokens are third-person report throughout, closing מְשַׁלֵּ֥ם גְּמ֖וּל לְאֹיְבָֽיו, against the second-person-plural address of oshb:Isa.66.5 (שִׁמְעוּ֙ token 1, אֲחֵיכֶ֨ם token 8, בְשִׂמְחַתְכֶ֖ם token 16, byte tier). The inventory records no petuchah or setumah at MT 66:5 or MT 66:6 and SAMEKH at MT 66:4 and MT 66:9 (single-witness, tier-3), so the shipped span's outer seams are independently bracketed and no respan arises. The row's own rejected alternative concedes the split is rejected 'not on the ground that no tier-1 signal divides them' and rests the rejection on content alone; a row that concedes a live verse-initial tier-1 rival inside its span and overrides it on content cannot carry 'high' with frontier_flag_considered false while sibling rows in this part flag softer, purely thematic tensions. The calibration claim is defective while the boundary itself is sound: medium, as filed. Non-span item; the proposed repair (confidence medium, flag true) is consistent with the bytes.

Re-derived at byte tier: oshb:Isa.66.15 (13 tokens) opens on כִּֽי (token 1) within כִּֽי הִנֵּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ (tokens 1-3), and oshb:Isa.66.14 closes on וְזָעַ֖ם אֶת אֹיְבָֽיו (tokens 12-14); the inventory records no petuchah or setumah at MT 66:14 or MT 66:15 and confirms SAMEKH at MT 66:11 and a paseq at MT 66:12 (count-only, single-witness), so the row's mark claims hold and the 66:14 | 66:15 seam rests, as its device_notes says, on the theophany onset alone. Neither boundary_rationale nor device_notes mentions the verse-initial connector, although the row's own WEB run “For, behold, Yahweh will come with fire” (web:Isa.66.15) begins with it; the same part discloses the identical construction at oshb:Isa.65.17 (כִּֽי, byte tier) as unmarked continuity the register shift is argued against. Adversarial check in the row's favour: the two-token opener spliced from oshb:Isa.66.15 recurs verse-initially at 4 verses book-wide (skeleton tier; MT 3:1, 26:21, 60:2, 66:15), so the connector belongs to a recurring theophany-onset formula and the seam survives -- which is why this is not high. But a byte-real causal link binding the onset to the row's closing clause, undisclosed at a single-leg seam with no mark, is a defective (incomplete) warrant rather than a mechanical omission: medium, as filed. Non-span item; the proposed disclosure repair is consistent with the bytes.
